abstract: The plant nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) immune receptors are known to play a crucial role in plant host defence against a variety of biotic stresses. Several NLR proteins contain integrated domains (NLR-ID) like ankyrin (ANK) and WRKY transcription factor domains and are important evolutionary adaptations in plant immunity. They are responsible for the perception of effector molecules from invading pathogens and pests and subsequent activation of plant immune responses. However, the functional roles these ANK-NLR-WRKY proteins play in wheat (Triticum aestivum) against various pathogens and pests remain poorly understood. Computational tools employed for comparative sequence and phylogenetic analyses revealed that TaAdnr1 is highly conserved across diploid (T. urartu), tetraploid (T. dicoccoides), and hexaploid (T. aestivum) wheat species, including its well characterised orthologue YrU1 from T. urartu. Three-dimensional (3D) protein structural modelling using AlphaFold2 supported strong conservation in the multiple domains of these NLR orthologues, more specifically within the integrated WRKY domain. This conservation may suggest a strong evolutionary maintenance of TaADNR1. Furthermore, this may also suggest TaADNR1 reflects specificity in effector recognition and regulation. Therefore, the integration of functional genomics studies, sequence analysis, evolutionary analysis and structural modelling possesses the potential to provide new insights into the pleiotropic roles of integrated domain NLRs in wheat.
